title: Electron Sandbox disallows launching appimages built in electron by the command line on Ubuntu
body:
On a system that doesn't support electron sandboxing (ubuntu w/ default apparmor configuration) launching appimages for programs made in electron via the command line results in a sandboxing error.

```
dadadah@Jacob-Maingear:~/Downloads/AppImage-x64$ ./Stoat-nightly-anylinux-x86_64.AppImage 
[9879:0818/173847.363937:FATAL:sandbox/linux/suid/client/setuid_sandbox_host.cc:166] The SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not configured correctly. Rather than run without sandboxing I'm aborting now. You need to make sure that /tmp/.mount_Stoatremp13161069797515101043/bin/chrome-sandbox is owned by root and has mode 4755.
```

Double clicking to launch the appimage works - is this because ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOXING is set to 1 in quick-sharun.sh? It'd be great if that behavior were carried over to the command line. Launching from CLI with `--no-sandbox` works as expected.

On this note - it may improve the security posture of electron appimages made with quick-sharun if electron sandboxing support were detected automatically on launch. There are some tools in the electron ecosystem that implement this automatically, but they're not widely used and not all electron apps will implement it (I'm working on implementing them into Stoat). See https://github.com/gergof/electron-builder-sandbox-fix . Perhaps combining the logic of checking for apparmor support seen in this linked repo and checking for kernel version (related to #438) will allow the appimages to run sandboxed when the system supports it, and unsandboxed when the system does not support it?

title: always ignore pipewire and spa libs in strace mode
body:
Libraries like SDL will always try to dlopen pipewire on the host. Which means during strace mode pipewire is added incompletly (`DEPLOY_PIPEWIRE` is not triggered here), and this is bad, because old versions of SDL2 have a bug that it considers pipewire audio as working if the libpipewire library exists: 

https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/issues/15924

Later on quick-sharun patches away the libpipewire strings so that SDL doesn't go and try to use the pipewire of the host.

For pipewire to be properly deployed, the `DEPLOY_PIPEWIRE=1` var needs to be set **and the `pipewire-audio` package needs to be installed in the CI runner**, otherwise audio will be broken.

title: implement `lib4bin` into `quick-sharun`, use our fork of sharun, use onelf instead of wrappe, and many more changes
body:
* Now `quick-sharun` uses our [fork of sharun](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/pull/662) with several new features.

* **One of features removes the `/bin/sh` dependency from the `AppRun`**, now sharun will try to use any `sh` or `bash` it can find on the host or AppDir if `/bin/sh` is not present.

* `sharun-aio`/`lib4bin` have been removed, deployment is done directly by `quick-sharun`

* `patchelf` is now a hard dependency of `quick-sharun` (needed to implement deployment)

* New variable: `QUICK_SHARUN_SKIP_DEPS_FOR`, which allows specifying libraries to skip dependency deployment.

* `--make-static-bin` now uses [onelf](https://github.com/qaidvoid/onelf) instead of wrappe.

* several workarounds have been removed now that they are properly fixed in our deployment steps.

* if pipewire does not get deployed, libraries will be patched to make sure they don't attempt to dlopen the pipewire of the host and crash.


# Breaking changes

Strace args are handled different now

Before you were able to run `quick-sharun /path/to/app -- google.com` and it would execute the app passing `google.com` as first argument

This has been replaced for the env variable `STRACE_BINARY` and `STRACE_FLAGS`

So now if you made use of this feature you have to declare the above env variables.

title: App request: Visual Studio Code
body:
Since there is no official MS AppImage package and let alone one made with sharun, it would be great to have it. While there exists stripped down [VSCodium](https://github.com/VSCodium/vscodium) version, sometimes it is required to have MS sync profile available across different devices. There is also [VSCode](https://github.com/valicm/VSCode-AppImage), but it is missing URL handler and packed with older appimagetool, that requires FUSE. 


They actually provide official `rpm` and `deb` packages via their repos https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux, which is great.

Another thing to note regarding app version tracking. Often electron apps hold app version number only in `resources/app/package.json` so on Linux almost always this will be missed. My suggestion would be to parse it during build time from there to `.desktop` as `X-AppImage-Version=`. Here is a script example I used:

```bash
# Extract version from Electron app's resources/app/package.json
# Used when no metainfo.xml exists (most Electron apps ship package.json instead)
if [ -n "$desktop_file_path" ]; then
    real_desktop_file=$(readlink -f "$desktop_file_path")
    if ! grep -q "^X-AppImage-Version=" "$real_desktop_file"; then
        package_json=$(find "$APPDIR" -path "*/resources/app/package.json" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$package_json" ]; then
            version=$(grep -m 1 -oE '"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' "$package_json" | sed 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')
            if [ -n "$version" ]; then
                echo "X-AppImage-Version=$version" >> "$real_desktop_file"
                echo "Added X-AppImage-Version=$version to desktop file (from Electron package.json)"
            fi
        fi
    fi
fi
```

title: Request: SecureCRT AppImage
body:
Hi, would it be possible to package SecureCRT as an AppImage?

SecureCRT is a professional terminal emulator and SSH client by VanDyke Software. While it is a commercial application, it is widely used by network engineers and developers. Having a portable AppImage would solve the persistent "dependency hell" encountered when moving between different Linux distributions (especially regarding older/newer SSL and Qt library versions).

Key Technical Requirements
To make the AppImage truly "universal" and user-friendly, I would like to request focus on the following two points during packaging:

Qt Theme Integration: SecureCRT is a Qt-based application. Please ensure the package includes necessary plugins (like qt5-style-plugins or libqgtk3.so) so it can inherit the host system's GTK or Kvantum themes. This avoids the "raw/ugly" default Qt look on modern desktops.

Fcitx5 Input Method Support: For many users, being able to input CJK characters is essential. Please ensure the libfcitx5platforminputcontextplugin.so (or the relevant Qt input context modules) is bundled and the environment variables are correctly configured so that Fcitx5 works out of the box.

App Info
Website: https://www.vandyke.com/products/securecrt/

Base Technology: Qt

Typical Install Path: /usr/bin/SecureCRT or /opt/vandyke/securecrt

Additional Notes
Since SecureCRT is commercial, the AppImage should ideally be a "portable builder" or an AppImage that expects the user to provide their own license/binary, OR a wrapper that packages the trial version which users can then activate.

Thank you for your amazing work on this repository!

title: Move locale-check logic into anylinux.so constructor, remove locale-check binary
body:
The locale fallback logic in `AppRun-generic` depended on a separately compiled static binary (`locale-check`) built at package time. This moves that logic into an `__attribute__((constructor))` in `anylinux.c`, so it runs automatically at `LD_PRELOAD` time — no extra binary needed.

### `useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c`
- Added new `init_locale()` constructor implementing the same fallback chain:
  1. `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` — if valid, return early
  2. Set `LOCPATH=$APPDIR/shared/lib/locale` if it exists, retry
  3. Fallback through `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` → `C.UTF-8` → `C`
- Uses `PATH_MAX` + `snprintf` truncation check for the `LOCPATH` construction

```c
__attribute__((constructor))
static void init_locale(void) {
    if (setlocale(LC_ALL, "")) return;  // already fine

    // try bundled locales
    const char *appdir = getenv("APPDIR");
    if (appdir) { /* set LOCPATH, retry */ }
    if (setlocale(LC_ALL, "")) return;

    // fallback chain
    const char *fallbacks[] = { "en_US.UTF-8", "C.UTF-8", "C", NULL };
    for (const char **fb = fallbacks; *fb; fb++) {
        setenv("LC_ALL", *fb, 1);
        if (setlocale(LC_ALL, "")) return;
    }
}
```

### `useful-tools/bin/AppRun-generic`
- Removed the `if command -v locale-check ...` block entirely (formerly lines 39–50)

### `useful-tools/quick-sharun.sh`
- Removed `_add_locale_check()` function, its call site, and the `LOCALE_CHECK` variable
- `DEBLOAT_LOCALE` / `LOCALE_DIR` are untouched (still used for locale data deployment)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Goal

Move the `locale-check` logic from the shell-based `AppRun-generic` into the `anylinux.c` shared library (as an `__attribute__((constructor))`), so locale checking happens automatically when `anylinux.so` is loaded. This eliminates the need to compile and ship a separate `locale-check` binary.

## Current implementation (3 files involved)

### 1. `useful-tools/quick-sharun.sh` — `_add_locale_check()` function (lines ~1228–1244)

This function compiles a tiny static binary `locale-check` into `$APPDIR/bin/locale-check`:

```c
#include <locale.h>
int main(void) { return setlocale(LC_ALL, "") ? 0 : 1; }
```

It is controlled by `LOCALE_CHECK=${LOCALE_CHECK:-1}` (line ~45).

### 2. `useful-tools/bin/AppRun-generic` — locale-check block (lines 39–50)

```sh
# check host locale works
if command -v locale-check 1>/dev/null && ! locale-check; then
	# use our locales
	__lcdir="$APPDIR"/shared/lib/locale
	[ ! -d "$__lcdir" ] || export LOCPATH="$__lcdir"
	# fallback to bundled en_US.UTF-8
	locale-check || export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8
	# fallback to bundled C.UTF-8
	locale-check || export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
	# fallback to bare C locale if this still fails somehow
	locale-check || export LC_ALL=C
fi
```

### 3. `useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c` — the shared library already loaded via `LD_PRELOAD`

This is a `.so` that is already `LD_PRELOAD`ed into every app. It already has multiple `__attribute__((constructor))` functions (`spoof_argv0`, `init_bindtextdomain_override`). It includes `<locale.h>` indirectly but can easily include it.

## Changes needed

### A. Add a new constructor to `useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c`

Add `#include <locale.h>` to the includes.

Add a new `__attribute__((constructor))` function that replicates the shell logic in C. The logic should be:

1. Try `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` — if it succeeds, locale is fine, return early.
2. If it fails, check if `$APPDIR/shared/lib/locale` exists and set `LOCPATH` to it.
3. Try `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` again — if it works now, done.
4. Fallback: `setenv("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8", 1)` then try `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")`.
5. Fallback: `setenv("LC_ALL", "C.UTF-8", 1)` then try `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")`.
6. Final fallback: `setenv("LC_ALL", "C", 1)`.

Use `DEBUG_PRINT` for logging each step (consistent with existing code style).

Use `stat()` or `access()` to check directory existence (the file already includes `<sys/types.h>`, `<unistd.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`).

**Important**: After the locale is fixed, call `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` one final time so the C runtime picks up the corrected environment. The constructor should also reset LC_ALL in the environment only if it was actually changed (don't clobber a user-provided LC_ALL).

### B. Remove the locale-check block from `useful-tools/bin/AppRun-generic`

Remove lines 39–50 (the entire `if command -v locale-check ...` block). The locale is now fixed automatically by the anylinux.so constructor before the app's `main()` runs.

### C. Remove `_add_locale_check()` from `useful-tools/quick-sharun.sh`

1. Remove the entire `_add_locale_check()` function (lines ~1228–1244).
2. Remove the call to `_add_locale_check` from the main deployment sequence (around line ~2376).
3. The `LOCALE_CHECK` variable declaration (line ~45) can also be removed since it's no longer needed.

title: AppImage template for Windows apps using `wine`
body:
It would be useful to have those so it's easier to package Windows apps in an AppImage.

There is some successful packaging of Windows apps in AppImages, like these:
https://github.com/mmtrt/foobar2000_AppImage
https://github.com/mmtrt/notepad-plus-plus_AppImage
https://github.com/ryuuzaki42/WinRAR_AppImage

So we would take that as an inspiration and do some work.
Base of the template would be this:  
https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/wine-AppImage

For the `wine` apps we can do the following:
- Set wineprefix to be inside the AppImage and `wineboot` it, so the data is populated (`$APPDIR/share/appname/`)
- Use `winetricks` to install app dependencies to that prefix if needed
- Set `%APPDATA%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%USERPROFILE%` and registry for the app data to be in r/w folder from the wine prefix (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/appname/`)
- Debloat it? (that would depend on per-app basis, so optional by the packager)
- Profit?

Question:
- Does Windows have equivalent of `strace`/`LD_DEBUG`, and `ldd`? So we can just have `quick-sharun`, but for Windows apps. Current `wineprefix` is bloated (around 400 MiB, not counting `wine` AppImage itself, where you would need to add around 144 MiB), where most apps only need minimal stuff from it. I guess that would be too much effort, but it would be nice to have.

Normally what we do is ship the `qt6ct`, `kvantum`, and now [lxqt-qtplugin](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/pavucontrol-qt-AppImage/commit/c3b8837666d0bb406f0492c4b64f99eb31785f6c) to allow applications to look native. `qt6-base` also ships `libqgtk3` by default which allows apps to use the host gtk3 theme. Adding all of these plugins usually increases the size of the app by about 1 MiB, so it is not a problem to include them always. 

The problem is that there is likely more plugins out there, not to mention new plugins that could exist in the future. And the person that packages the appimage needs to be aware to install these packages so that the plugins get included.

I also had an issue at Eden with one user wondering why their qt6ct theme was working, and it was because they were using [a fork of qt6ct](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/qt6ct-kde) which themes are not compatible with `qt6ct`.

---

This pretty much means that a patch has to be written and shipped to Qt to allow loading additional platform theme plugin on the host thru an env variable, this would also need to perform sanity checks to prevents apps from crashing if the plugins are not compatible.

title: merge `uruntime2appimage` into `quick-sharun`
body:
`_make_appimage()` previously downloaded and `exec`'d `uruntime2appimage.sh` at runtime, duplicating logic already present in `quick-sharun.sh` and conflating real machine arch (`uname -m`) with user-overridable artifact naming (`$ARCH`).

## Changes

### New `APPIMAGE_ARCH` variable
- Added `APPIMAGE_ARCH="$(uname -m)"` alongside `ARCH` at the top of the script
- `APPIMAGE_ARCH` = real machine arch, used for binary downloads and metadata — never user-overridden
- `ARCH` = artifact naming, UPINFO zsync patterns — can be overridden by the user

### Fixed `$ARCH` → `$APPIMAGE_ARCH` references
| Location | Reason |
|---|---|
| `SHARUN_LINK` download URL | Binary must match real machine arch |
| `LIB_DIR` detection (`/usr/lib/$ARCH-linux-gnu`) | Detecting actual system lib dir |
| Hook x86_64 arch guard | Checking if machine can run x86_64 hooks |
| `@APPIMAGE_ARCH@` substitution in AppRun | Embedding real arch |

### New top-level overridable variables (from uruntime2appimage.sh)
Added alongside existing vars so users can override via env, matching the established pattern:
```sh
OUTPATH, DWARFS_COMP, DWARFS_CMD, RUNTIME, DWARFSPROF,
OPTIMIZE_LAUNCH, URUNTIME_LINK, DWARFS_LINK
```

### `_make_appimage()` fully inlined
Removed the download + `exec` of `uruntime2appimage.sh`. The function now directly contains:
- AppDir/AppRun validation
- Desktop entry metadata injection (`X-AppImage-Name/Version/Arch` using `$APPIMAGE_ARCH`)
- Icon resolution via `_find_dir_icon()` — shallow top-level search, then deep hicolor dir search
- `OUTNAME` construction using `$ARCH`, `UPINFO` guessing from `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` using `$ARCH`
- mkdwarfs/uruntime download, `URUNTIME_PRELOAD`, `ADD_PERMA_ENV_VARS` injection
- `.env` unset-sorting (needed for the `--make-appimage` standalone path where main-flow sorting hasn't run)
- mkdwarfs invocation with `OPTIMIZE_LAUNCH` profiling support
- zsync + `appinfo` output

### New `_find_dir_icon()` function
The `.DirIcon`-finding logic has been extracted into a standalone `_find_dir_icon()` function called from both `_sanity_check` and `_make_appimage`:
- **`_sanity_check`**: when `OUTPUT_APPIMAGE=1` and no explicit `$ICON` is set, `_find_dir_icon` runs before the heavy `_deploy_libs` work — failing early if no icon source is available
- **`_make_appimage`**: covers the `--make-appimage` path (which skips `_sanity_check`) and the case where `$ICON` is set (the icon is deployed into APPDIR by `_deploy_icon_and_desktop` before `_make_appimage` runs)

`uruntime2appimage.sh` is left untouched for users who invoke it standalone.

##### Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in `actions/upload-artifact`, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the `Content-Type` header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. After https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/issues/14887 we may want to have a better method to block certain libraries from loading.

For example: 

* gtk3 apps sometimes need to dlopen mesa for some reason, even though it is not needed for their operation at all (gtk3 is not hardware accelerated) and work fine when not found, but if mesa is not added then they will try to dlopen the mesa of the host which can cause a crash.

* Many qt6 and gtk4 apps work fine without hardware accel, [example](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Keypunch-AppImage/pull/5)

* [This app](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/SuperTux-AppImage-Enhanced) for some reason always tries to dlopen pipewire ignoring the `SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER` env vars, it works perfectly fine when it doesn't find it.

title: Refactor HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md: Add quick-sharun guide and practical examples
body:
The documentation was written before `quick-sharun` and AppImage templates existed, providing only theoretical explanations without practical guidance.

## Changes

**New Quick Start Guide** (added ~200 lines)
- Prerequisites, basic workflow, and step-by-step examples
- Code snippets for GTK, Qt, and OpenGL/Vulkan applications
- Debloated packages integration

```bash
export ANYLINUX_LIB=1
export DEPLOY_OPENGL=1
./quick-sharun /usr/bin/myapp
./quick-sharun --make-appimage
```

**Hooks Documentation**
- Complete reference of 7 available hooks (self-updater, fix-namespaces, udev-installer, etc.)
- Usage patterns with `ADD_HOOKS` variable

**Environment Variables Reference**
- 30+ variables documented with categories: Basic, Deployment, Library handling, Locale, Python, Advanced
- Default values and behavior specified

**Examples and Templates Section**
- Links to 4 demo scripts and 3 production repositories
- Ready-to-use template structure

**Content Restructuring**
- Moved theoretical content under "Understanding the approach" with note that quick-sharun automates these details
- Updated table of contents for better navigation
- Fixed grammar errors and formatting issues (missing backtick, unclear GPU reference)

The document now serves both quick-start users and those seeking technical depth, with practical examples preceding theory.

I use Gitea for development, and I also use Gitea Action to automatically create releases with all packages, since Gitea Action is backward compatible with GitHub Actions. Condition 

```

if [ -z “$UPINFO” ]; then
    >&2 echo “No update information given, trying to guess it...”
	if [ -n “$GITHUB_REPOSITORY” ]; then
        UPINFO="gh-releases-zsync|${GITHUB_REPOSITORY%/*}|${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}|latest|*$ARCH.AppImage.zsync"
		>&2 echo
        >&2 echo “Guessed $UPINFO as the update information”
        >&2 echo “It may be wrong so please set the UPINFO instead”
        >&2 echo
	else
        >&2 echo
        >&2 echo “We were not able to guess the update information”
        >&2 echo “Please add it if you will distribute the AppImage”
        >&2 echo
    fi
fi

```

It works and installs gh-releases-zsync, since gitea doesn't seem to have a latest link, I didn't install upinfo. Accordingly, I would like it not to be installed at all, but now it turns out that it is trying to refer to a non-existent git.

### [`v5.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v5.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v4.3.0...v5.0.0)

#### What's Changed

- Update README.md by [@​nebuk89](https://redirect.github.com/nebuk89) in [#​407](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/407)
- BREAKING fix: inconsistent path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID by [@​GrantBirki](https://redirect.github.com/GrantBirki) in [#​416](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/416)

#### v5.0.0

##### 🚨 Breaking Change

This release fixes an inconsistency in path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID. **If you're downloading single artifacts by ID, the output path may change.**

##### What Changed

Previously, **single artifact downloads** behaved differently depending on how you specified the artifact:

- **By name**: `name: my-artifact` → extracted to `path/` (direct)
- **By ID**: `artifact-ids: 12345` → extracted to `path/my-artifact/` (nested)

Now both methods are consistent:

- **By name**: `name: my-artifact` → extracted to `path/` (unchanged)
- **By ID**: `artifact-ids: 12345` → extracted to `path/` (fixed - now direct)

##### Migration Guide

##### ✅ No Action Needed If:

- You download artifacts by **name**
- You download **multiple** artifacts by ID
- You already use `merge-multiple: true` as a workaround

##### ⚠️ Action Required If:

You download **single artifacts by ID** and your workflows expect the nested directory structure.

**Before v5 (nested structure):**

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    artifact-ids: 12345
    path: dist

### Files were in: dist/my-artifact/
```

> Where `my-artifact` is the name of the artifact you previously uploaded

**To maintain old behavior (if needed):**

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
  with:
    artifact-ids: 12345
    path: dist/my-artifact  # Explicitly specify the nested path
```

- [@​nebuk89](https://redirect.github.com/nebuk89) made their first contribution in [#​407](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/407)

body:
This afternoon I was trying to build an appimage for ePSXe, so I downloaded the latest version from the official site and tried to built it, but I ran into some issues with ncurses and other libs like libcurl, specially libcurl, because the version that ePSXe wants is a very specific one

However, somewhere on github the appimage is already made, but it's an "old school" appimage, so the GLIBC limit is a problem for me specifically, because I am using an old system. So I downloaded that appimage, extracted it, and I tried making a new one by giving quick-sharun.sh a custom $LIB_DIR to the "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu" inside the original AppDir and gave it the binary (which is the exact same as the official one btw)

Once the new AppImage was done, I ran it and it threw an error saying that one of its ncurses library is missing. The quick-sharun.sh script recognized most of the libraries inside the provided AppDir but it completely ignored some libraries, ncurses is one of them, but it may have ignored more than that, so what I wanna know is:

I want to add EXPLICITLY all of those libraries from the already existing AppImage, because those dependencies are already there. How do I do this with quick-sharun.sh ? I looked at the --help but didn't find anything that would do anything like that

This script is a simplified version how everything happened:

```
NAME="ePSXe"
ARCH= "x86_64"
VERSION="2.0.5"

./epsxe_2.0.5_made_by_someone_else.AppImage --appimage-extract

mv -v squashfs-root AppDir.old

PATH_DESKTOP=$(realpath -e ./AppDir.old/ePSXe_2.0.5.desktop)
PATH_ICON=$(realpath -e ./AppDir.old/epsxe.png)
PATH_LIBS=$(realpath -e ./AppDir.old/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu)
PATH_MAINBIN=$(realpath -e ./AppDir.old/usr/bin/epsxe_x64)

export OUTNAME="$NAME"_v"$VERSION"_AnyLinux_"$ARCH".AppImage
export DESKTOP="$PATH_DESKTOP"
export ICON="$PATH_ICON"

export LIB_DIR="$PATH_LIBS"

./quick-sharun.sh "$PATH_MAINBIN"

./uruntime2appimage.sh

```

And like I said, it creates the appimage, but it throws that libncurses was not found when it clearly is inside the LIB_DIR that I provided

I also want to clarify that my main system is an old system, but this entire work I'm trying to do with these AnyLinux appimages is in a chrooted ArchLinux that I set up a couple of days ago with arch-chroot and it is up to date with no issues so far

This is not complete, we still need hardcoded path mapping with relative symlinks in `/tmp` because: 

* `_deploy_locale` func checks for `grep -Eaoq -m 1 "/usr/share/locale" ` on every binary and if it detects a harcoded path to locales it does binary patching.

If I were to replace this for pathmap, **all libraries** would try to find locales in the AppDir, which is likely going to cause issues.

* Some apps also have hardcoded paths to `/usr/share/icons`, those I cannot use pathmap easily because it means again that all libraries would try to find icons in the AppDir which is likely going to break custom theming.

title: Improve relative path mapping

WIth this trick,  when relative path mapping is used the current working dir gets restored to the original value.

It works this way: 

* When `PATH_MAPPING_RELATIVE` is set the env var `ORIGINAL_WORKING_DIR=${PWD}` is set along with the original `SHARUN_WORKING_DIR=${SHARUN_DIR}`.

* `exec.so` will check if `ORIGINAL_WORKING_DIR` and if so it will set the working dir to it.

* This means path mapping relative is less problematic, for example when you go to open a new file or another application the working dir will no longer be the wierd `/tmp/.mount*` location. Of course this is not perfect since some apps display their working dir internally and in that case there is no solution yet.

Also fixed the patching functions to do relative patching when `PATH_MAPPING_RELATIVE` is in use, this way both methods don't get used together.

title: Fix AppImage portable home/config handling with precise XDG variable detection
body:
## Problem

The current implementation of `exec.c` in useful-tools does not properly handle AppImage's portable home and portable config features. When AppImage sets environment variables to portable locations, child processes inherit incorrect paths instead of using the real system directories.

This causes external processes launched from an AppImage to operate with wrong directories, leading to issues where:
- Configuration files are read from/written to the wrong location  
- User data is stored in temporary AppImage-specific directories
- External tools can't access the user's actual home directory

## Solution

This PR adds functionality to detect and restore original environment values when launching external processes while properly respecting the XDG Base Directory specification:

### Precise Portable Directory Detection

The implementation uses **exact pattern matching** to identify AppImage portable directories:

- **HOME**: Detects when `HOME` ends with `.home` suffix (indicating `$APPIMAGE.home` pattern)
- **XDG_CONFIG_HOME**: Detects when it exactly equals `$APPIMAGE.config` (not just any path ending in `.config`)
- **XDG_DATA_HOME**: Detects when it exactly equals `$APPIMAGE.share` (not just any path ending in `.share`)

This ensures normal XDG directories like `/home/user/.config` are **not** incorrectly treated as portable AppImage directories.

### XDG Variable Handling (Key Fix)

The implementation properly handles `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` according to XDG specification:

- **When parent process had XDG variables set**: Restores to original parent values
- **When parent process didn't have XDG variables set**: Unsets AppImage portable variants so applications use standard defaults (`~/.config`, `~/.local/share`)
- **Never interferes with normal XDG paths**: Only processes actual `$APPIMAGE.config`/`$APPIMAGE.share` patterns

### Implementation Details

The fix uses a **multi-tiered approach** to find original environment values:

1. **Primary**: Read from parent process environment via `/proc/[ppid]/environ`
2. **Fallback**: Get real home directory from `passwd` database for HOME only
3. **Tracking**: Distinguish between "parent had variable set" vs "parent didn't have variable set"
4. **Precise Detection**: Match exact `$APPIMAGE` patterns rather than suffix checking

### Testing

```bash
# Test 1: Normal XDG_CONFIG_HOME="/home/user/.config"
# Result: NOT treated as portable → Left unchanged

# Test 2: Portable XDG_CONFIG_HOME="/path/to/app.AppImage.config"  
# Parent didn't have XDG_CONFIG_HOME set
# Result: Variable unset → app uses ~/.config default

# Test 3: Portable XDG_CONFIG_HOME="/path/to/app.AppImage.config"
# Parent had XDG_CONFIG_HOME="/custom/path"
# Result: Restored to "/custom/path"
```

The implementation is surgical and maintains full backward compatibility while ensuring external tools work correctly with user's actual configuration and data directories, without interfering with normal XDG directory usage.
